blocks.text: Exodus 38 represents the construction phase of Exodus's two-part sanctuary narrative. After the detailed instructions of Exodus 25-27, this chapter describes the actual fabrication and assembly of the sanctuary's components—the altar of burnt offering, the laver, and the court. The chapter's extensive attention to measurements, materials, and specifications reflects a deliberate literary pattern: detailed instruction followed by documented compliance and completion. This emphasis on authorized construction and careful execution underscores the sanctioned nature of the work and its completion as central to Exodus's portrayal of the tabernacle narrative.
